title: Total synthesis of a novel C9-monoterpenoid alkaloid, Forsyqinlingine C, and its therapeutic potential in sepsis-induced acute lung injury via modulation of the TLR4/TRIF/NF-kappaB pathway.
authors: Xin, Jianzeng; Sun, Yupei; Huang, Shuai; Yang, Pufan; Mou, Xiaofeng; Dai, Shengjun; Du, Yuan; Liu, Sheng
one_liner_zh: 该文为天然产物全合成及脓毒症肺损伤抗炎机制研究，涉及TLR4/NF-kappaB通路和分子对接，但无蛋白质-DNA互作体系，与本课题无关。
abstract: Sepsis-induced acute lung injury (ALI) is a critical health concern with high morbidity and mortality, while its effective treatment options are limited. Our previous study, identified forsyqinlingine C (FC), a novel C9-monoterpenoid alkaloid from the ripe fruit of Forsythia suspensa (Thunb.) Vahl, exhibits notable anti-inflammatory activity. In this study, we reported the total synthesis of FC and its therapeutic potential against sepsis-induced ALI for the first time. The target compound was achieved in four steps, including barbier reaction, heck reaction, hydroxyl reduction and hydroboration oxidation, with impressive combined yields of 45 % and high purity of 95 %. In biological study, an inflammatory cell model and a murine model of sepsis-induced ALI were established to explore the potential protective effect of FC and its underlying mechanisms. Our findings indicated that FC could inhibit the expression levels of TLR4, TRIF, p-NF-kappaB p65, and p-IkappaB-alpha and reduce the production of downstream inflammatory cytokine (IL-6 and TNF-alpha) in MLE-12 cells. In vivo, FC significantly alleviates LPS-induced lung injury by reducing MPO levels, and lung W/D ratios, and ameliorating histopathological alterations. FC also decreased TNF-alpha and IL-6 production induced by LPS in the murine serum, BALF, and lung tissue in a dose-dependent manner. Meanwhile, FC inhibited the expression levels of TLR4, TRIF, p-NF-kappaB p65, and p-IkappaB-alpha, which are activated by LPS administration. Furthermore, molecular docking studies results speculated that FC could disturb the TLR4/TRIF signaling pathway. In conclusion, FC demonstrated potential in alleviating sepsis-induced ALI, primarily by inhibiting LPS-stimulated inflammatory response through the TLR4/TRIF/NF-kappaB signaling pathway. This research offers an alternative treatment for sepsis-induced ALI.
abstract_zh: 脓毒症诱导的急性肺损伤（ALI）是一个具有高发病率和死亡率的重大健康问题，而其有效治疗选择有限。我们先前的研究发现，连翘辛碱C（FC）是一种从连翘（Forsythia suspensa (Thunb.) Vahl）成熟果实中提取的新型C9-单萜生物碱，具有显著的抗炎活性。在本研究中，我们首次报道了FC的全合成及其对脓毒症诱导的ALI的治疗潜力。目标化合物通过四步反应合成，包括巴比耶反应、赫克反应、羟基还原和硼氢化氧化，总收率高达45%，纯度达95%。在生物学研究中，建立了炎症细胞模型和脓毒症诱导的ALI小鼠模型，以探讨FC的潜在保护作用及其潜在机制。我们的研究结果表明，FC能抑制MLE-12细胞中TLR4、TRIF、p-NF-kappaB p65和p-IkappaB-alpha的表达水平，并减少下游炎症细胞因子（IL-6和TNF-alpha）的产生。在体内实验中，FC通过降低MPO水平、肺湿干比（W/D比值）以及改善组织病理学变化，显著减轻了LPS诱导的肺损伤。FC还以剂量依赖性方式降低了LPS诱导的小鼠血清、支气管肺泡灌洗液（BALF）和肺组织中TNF-alpha和IL-6的产生。同时，FC抑制了由LPS给药激活的TLR4、TRIF、p-NF-kappaB p65和p-IkappaB-alpha的表达水平。此外，分子对接研究结果推测FC可能干扰TLR4/TRIF信号通路。总之，FC显示出缓解脓毒症诱导的ALI的潜力，主要通过抑制LPS刺激的炎症反应，经由TLR4/TRIF/NF-kappaB信号通路实现。本研究为脓毒症诱导的ALI提供了一种替代治疗方案。
